claim: § The three axes: every text event is a point in (source, diegesis, addressee) carrying an emotion, and the presentation is a function of those four, not a free style choice; source outranks emotion.

pieces.what: Set the four answers (source, diegesis, addressee, emotion) and the balloon, tail, face and placement are chosen for you; set a menacing radio and see source win.
The who's-talking proof: read the answers back off the form alone.
The conversation ladder: rules one per frame, each fix beside its mistake under a computed checker, the pause left as the one the checker can't see.
